edges.description: DNM2-dependent membrane-trafficking failure impairs both Schwann-cell and axonal homeostasis, converging on the mixed intermediate lesion.
Impaired tRNA aminoacylation compromises protein synthesis in long peripheral neurons, converging on the intermediate demyelinating-and-axonal lesion.
Disrupted Gβ4-related GPCR signaling in peripheral nerve converges on the mixed intermediate lesion.
Loss of myelin protein zero from compact myelin degrades the myelin sheath and, through MPZ's allele-dependent axonal effects, converges on the mixed intermediate lesion.
Because GDAP1 loss impairs axonal integrity and Schwann-cell properties at the same time, the resulting nerve pathology is mixed rather than predominantly demyelinating or predominantly axonal.

edges.description: Loss of PLEKHG5 from both the neuronal and the glial compartment of peripheral nerve converges on the mixed intermediate lesion, measured as reduced nerve conduction velocity in patients and in knockout mice.

nodes.description: Mutations in the aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases YARS1 (tyrosyl-tRNA synthetase, DI-CMTC) and KARS1 (lysyl-tRNA synthetase, RI-CMTB) partially impair tRNA-charging (aminoacylation) activity and, for YARS1, mislocalize the enzyme within the axon. Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase impairment is a recurrent CMT mechanism, predominantly producing axonal pathology, and here yields the intermediate phenotype.

nodes.description: The shared terminal node of the intermediate CMT compartment. The diverse upstream lesions (DNM2 membrane-remodelling failure, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase dysfunction, GNB4 signaling defect, MPZ compact-myelin structural failure, GDAP1 loss of axonal and Schwann-cell integrity, and PLEKHG5 deficiency in peripheral nerve neurons and glia) converge on peripheral nerve pathology that combines demyelination and length-dependent axonal degeneration — the combination that produces the intermediate nerve conduction velocities defining this compartment and the progressive distal deficit shared with the CMT1 and CMT2 compartments.

evidence.snippet: we identified unique mutations in dynamin 2 (DNM2) in all families. DNM2 belongs to the family of large GTPases and is part of the cellular fusion-fission apparatus.

nodes.description: Mutations in DNM2 (DI-CMTB) impair dynamin-2, a large GTPase of the membrane fission-fusion machinery that mediates membrane scission during endocytosis and vesicle trafficking. Disrupted DNM2-dependent membrane remodeling in Schwann cells and neurons produces a mixed demyelinating-and-axonal (intermediate) neuropathy.

evidence.snippet: Homozygosity for a single base pair insertion in exon 3 (c.349_350insT) was observed in affected children from a Turkish inbred pedigree.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the ganglioside-induced differentiation-associated protein-1 (GDAP1) gene in intermediate type autosomal recessive Charcot-Marie-Tooth neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Nerve conduction velocities were between 25 and 35 m/s and peripheral nerve pathology showed axonal as well as demyelinating changes. These findings fitted the definition of intermediate type CMT and further support the view that GDAP1 is vital for both, axonal integrity and Schwann cell properties.

nodes.description: Biallelic GDAP1 loss-of-function alleles (RI-CMTA) compromise peripheral nerve on both sides of the axon-glia partnership: nerve pathology in intermediate-type GDAP1 families shows axonal degeneration together with demyelinating change, which is why GDAP1 alleles can present as axonal, demyelinating or intermediate neuropathy.

evidence.snippet: Myelin protein zero is a key structural component of compact myelin, and over 100 mutations in this protein have been reported, which can give rise to neuropathies with either axonal, demyelinating, or intermediate features encompassing a wide range of severity.

nodes.description: Heterozygous MPZ mutations (DI-CMTD) disrupt myelin protein zero, the major structural glycoprotein of compact peripheral-nerve myelin made by Schwann cells. Different MPZ alleles shift the balance between demyelinating and axonal pathology; the intermediate presentation shows mild demyelinating features with conduction velocities in the intermediate range.

evidence.snippet: Interestingly, a homozygous PLEKHG5 missense mutation was previously reported in a recessive form of severe childhood onset lower motor neuron disease (LMND) leading to loss of the ability to walk and need for respiratory assistance.

nodes.description: Biallelic PLEKHG5 null alleles (RI-CMTC) remove a protein expressed in both the neurons and the glial cells of the peripheral nervous system. Plekhg5 knockout mice reproduce the reduced nerve conduction velocities seen in affected individuals, and the same gene produces a severe childhood-onset lower motor neuron disease with other genotypes.
